plan.planning_summary: This portfolio tests three distinct strategy axes for a dual-band filter: (1) a periodic Bragg stack centered on the visible stopband, (2) a chirped thickness-modulated stack to broaden visible rejection, and (3) a defect-cavity stack to sharpen telecom transmission. These axes are genuinely different because they rely on different physical mechanisms - Bragg interference versus graded index versus cavity resonance - and can succeed or fail independently. The 30-layer constraint is respected in all routes. Literature L02, L18, L34 support periodic and optimization approaches; L04 supports thickness modulation; L03, L15, L33 address HfO2/SiO2 coating durability relevant to space applications. No route optimizes refractive index; all tune geometry only.

routes.title: Periodic Bragg Stack Centered on Visible Stopband
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A quarter-wave Bragg stack with 7 HfO2/SiO2 pairs centered at 550 nm will achieve high visible reflectance while maintaining adequate telecom transmittance, with performance improving monotonically as pair count increases up to the 30-layer limit.
routes.design_principle: Bragg interference from periodic high-low index contrasts creates a photonic stopband centered at the design wavelength; quarter-wave optical thickness maximizes reflectance bandwidth for a given pair count.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | (HfO2 | SiO2) x 7 | Fused Silica substrate
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 14 layers
Center wavelength of the quarter-wave condition
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 400-700 nm band
Minimize layer count while meeting performance targets
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 14 (well under 30-layer limit)
Quarter-wave thicknesses are manufacturable with standard deposition control
HfO2/SiO2 pair is space-qualified per L03, L15, L33
theory_basis: Bragg reflector theory for 1D photonic crystals
Quarter-wave stack design for maximum stopband reflectance
known_risks: Stopband may not cover full 400-700 nm range with only 7 pairs
Telecom transmittance may suffer from residual stopband tails
Limited design freedom compared to non-periodic approaches
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 14-layer periodic Bragg stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand) (7 pairs, high-index layer first). Optimize individual layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band and reflectance in 400-700 nm band. Initial thicknesses set to quarter-wave optical thickness at 550 nm center wavelength. Materials: hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) from catalog. Substrate: SiO2 (Lemarchand) (fused silica). Incident medium: air. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized light.

routes.title: Chirped Thickness-Modulated Stack for Broadband Visible Rejection
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A chirped stack with systematically varying layer thicknesses across 24 layers will achieve broader visible stopband coverage than a periodic stack while maintaining telecom transmittance, because thickness grading extends the effective stopband width.
routes.design_principle: Varying the optical thickness of successive pairs shifts the local Bragg condition, creating overlapping stopbands that merge into a wider composite rejection band; this is the principle behind thickness-modulated designs in L04.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (24 layers, 12 pairs)
design_variables: Thickness progression pattern across the 24 layers
Base center wavelength for the chirp sequence
soft_objectives: Maximize mean reflectance across full 400-700 nm band
Maintain transmittance above threshold in 1530-1565 nm band
Minimize ripple in telecom transmission band
manufacturing_considerations: 24 layers uses 80 percent of the 30-layer budget, leaving margin for future refinement
Thickness variation must remain within deposition tool capability
HfO2/SiO2 system has demonstrated durability in space environments per L03, L15
theory_basis: Chirped Bragg reflector theory for broadband stopbands
expected_advantages: Broader visible stopband than periodic stack
Can tailor transition region between visible and telecom bands
known_risks: More complex optimization landscape with more local minima
May require more iterations to converge
Thickness extremes could approach manufacturability limits
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 24-layer chirped stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: alternating HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) starting with HfO2 (12 pairs total). Optimize layer thicknesses with a chirp constraint where thickness varies systematically from layer 1 to layer 24. Initial thicknesses follow a linear chirp from quarter-wave at 450 nm (first pair) to quarter-wave at 650 nm (last pair). Materials: hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) from catalog. Substrate: SiO2 (Lemarchand) (fused silica). Incident medium: air. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Optimize for maximum reflectance in 400-700 nm and maximum transmittance in 1530-1565 nm.

routes.title: Defect-Cavity Stack for Sharp Telecom Transmission Peak
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Introducing a half-wave defect cavity within a Bragg reflector will create a narrow transmission peak at 1550 nm while maintaining high visible reflectance, because the defect creates a resonant mode within the photonic bandgap.
routes.design_principle: A defect layer (typically half-wave optical thickness) breaks the periodicity of a Bragg stack, creating a localized resonant state that allows transmission at the defect wavelength while the surrounding Bragg mirrors maintain high reflectance elsewhere.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | (HfO2 | SiO2) x 5 | HfO2 (defect) | (SiO2 | HfO2) x 5 | Fused Silica substrate (21 layers total: 10 pairs plus one defect layer)
design_variables: Defect layer position within the stack
Thicknesses of the surrounding Bragg mirror pairs
soft_objectives: Maximize transmittance peak at 1550 nm center of telecom band
Minimize transmission bandwidth to reduce out-of-band leakage
manufacturing_considerations: 21 layers uses 70 percent of the 30-layer budget
Defect thickness control is critical for peak wavelength accuracy
HfO2/SiO2 defect cavities have been demonstrated in high-power laser applications per L09, L15
theory_basis: Defect mode theory in 1D photonic crystals
Cavity resonance in distributed Bragg reflectors
expected_advantages: Very sharp transmission peak at telecom wavelength
Excellent visible rejection from strong Bragg mirrors
Defect position provides additional design degree of freedom
known_risks: Transmission peak may be too narrow for full 1530-1565 nm band
Defect layer thickness tolerance is critical
May require more mirror pairs to achieve sufficient visible reflectance
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 21-layer defect-cavity stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: 5 HfO2/SiO2 (Lemarchand) pairs, then one HfO2 defect layer, then 5 SiO2 (Lemarchand)/HfO2 pairs (mirror symmetry around defect). Optimize defect layer thickness to center transmission peak at 1550 nm, and optimize surrounding mirror pair thicknesses for maximum visible reflectance. Initial defect thickness set to half-wave optical thickness at 1550 nm. Materials: hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) from catalog. Substrate: SiO2 (Lemarchand) (fused silica). Incident medium: air. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized light.
